modern: When you are offended at any man’s fault, immediately turn to yourself and reflect in what similar way you err yourself; for example, in thinking that money is a good thing, or pleasure, or a bit of reputation, and the like. For by attending to this you will quickly forget your anger, if this thought is also added, that the man is compelled: for what else could he do? Or, if you are able, take away the compulsion from him.
original: When thou art offended at any man’s fault, forthwith turn to thyself and reflect in what like manner thou dost err thyself; for example, in thinking that money is a good thing, or pleasure, or a bit of reputation, and the like. For by attending to this thou wilt quickly forget thy anger, if this consideration also is added, that the man is compelled: for what else could he do? or, if thou art able, take away from him the compulsion.

explained.summary:
When someone’s fault annoys you, look straight at your own similar faults, such as treating money, pleasure or a bit of reputation as if they were truly good. That quickly takes the heat out of your anger.

It helps, too, to remember that the other person is acting under compulsion: given what they believe, what else could they do? And if you can, help free them from the mistaken belief that drives them.
explained.today: When a colleague grabs the credit, remember the times you angled for a mention yourself. When a driver cuts you up, recall the days you were the one in a rush. Anger fades fast once you spot the same weakness at home.
